**Job Description**
-------------------


New York City Emergency Management (NYCEM) helps New Yorkers before, during, and after emergencies through preparedness, education, and response. NYCEM is responsible for coordinating citywide emergency planning and response for all types and scales of emergencies. We are staffed by more than 200 dedicated professionals with diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise, including individuals assigned from other City agencies.
  

  

The Office of the Chief Financial Officer is responsible for the oversight, management, accounting, and reporting of all agency funds, as well as the procurement planning, development, implementation, and management of all agency contracts.
  

The Procurement Unit is responsible for providing management, oversight, review, and support of all procurement functions at NYCEM. NYCEM procurements are governed by the City Charter and the City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules.
  

  

Reporting to the Assistant Commissioner for Administration \& Finance/ACCO, responsibilities include, but are not limited to: overseeing all contracting actions and vendor selection process, conferring with the ACCO and advising agency staff on appropriate procurement methodology and applicability of local procurement law, supervising procurement staff, reviewing solicitations and proposals, approving oversight documents such as pre\-solicitation reports, recommendations for awards and request for renewals, and approving purchase orders and contracts in FMS.
  

  

The Deputy Agency Chief Contracting Officer (DACCO) will:
  

* Review and monitor agency procurement actions and contracting functions to ensure compliance with the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) rules and all other applicable city, state, and federal requirements.

  

* Oversee and manage procurements, varying in size and complexity, that focus on emergency events and citywide initiatives; ensure that multiple Program Unit needs are met in a timely manner; ensure that vendors understand Agency requirements and process flows.

  

* Approve Pre\-Solicitation Report (PSRs), Recommendations for Award (RFAs), Responsibility Determinations (RDs) and other forms/information as required by the procurement process; oversee evaluation of submitted proposals; determine vendor responsiveness and responsibility; provide support in establishing and monitoring timelines for these tasks.

  

* Assist in drafting specifications/scopes of work; reviews and approves contract specifications before advertising to ensure conformity to the agency’s requirements and federal/state/city mandates; ensure proper content and format of Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and other solicitation documents.

  

* Monitor and update a variety of reports on the status of small and large\-scale procurement plans for submission to oversight agencies.

  

* Approve requirements contract; purchase orders in FMS and/or PASSPort; submit contracts and task orders to the Comptroller’s Office for registration; track purchasing activity for management reporting and analysis.

  

* In the absence of the ACCO serve as the point of contact with the Mayor’s Office of Contract Services (MOCS); represent the agency at citywide ACCO meetings and relevant public hearings; research Division of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) requirements contracts and State/federal contracting opportunities; consult with other City agencies on best practices and recommended vendors.

  

\*\*PLEASE NOTE THE FOLLOWING:
  

  

* As part of NYCEM's emergency response mission, this position participates in an Emergency Operations Center (EOC) team. During emergency activations, team members may be required to work evenings, weekends, holidays, or extended shifts in support of City response operations. Outside of activations, EOC members participate in periodic training and exercises to maintain operational readiness, and must volunteer to assist with three Ready NY emergency preparedness presentations per year. EOC teams are on call for three weeks at a time, with six weeks off in between.

  

* Please note, the high end of the salary range is available to candidates who have been in City service two or more years.

  

Funding – This position is supported with a federal Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI) grant funding through 8/31/2027 with the possibility of an extension.
  

  

* Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without employer support to be eligible for selection. Note that NYCEM does not participate in eVerify, which is required for the reauthorization of some visas.

  

* The selected candidate will be required to be in person in the office location three days per week, with exceptions for extenuating circumstances.

  

* We as an agency recognize that valuable leadership and analytical experience may be gained through public service, military service, academia, nonprofit organizations, the private sector, volunteer leadership, or other professional settings. Candidates are encouraged to describe transferable experiences that demonstrate their qualifications.

  

* NYCEM is committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the application and hiring process for qualified applicants with disabilities.

The above hiring range represents the University's good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.*  

Position Summary


Reporting to the Associate Dean of Students and Registration Services, the Executive Director and Registrar serves as the lead administrator for the Office of Registration Services (ORS) at Columbia Law School. The Registrar leads a dedicated team of higher education professionals responsible for academic policy implementation, registration operations, recordkeeping, exam administration, grade tracking, graduation clearance, and strict regulatory compliance (including ABA standards, NYS Bar requirements, and FERPA). Working closely with the Office of the Vice Dean of Academic Affairs, the Office of Student Services, the Office of Graduate Degree Programs and other Law School and University partners, the Registrar ensures data integrity across institutional databases while driving digital transformation to enhance student\-facing and administrative workflows to ensure a positive, efficient, and professional student learning experience.


Responsibilities


**Academic Operations \& Registration Management (30%)**


* Lead biannual registration, course lottery allocations, cross\-registration (including Columbia Graduate Schools such as Columbia Business School (CBS) and the School for International and Public Affairs (SIPA), and the Columbia/NYU Exchange Program)), and add/drop processes.
* Manage course setup and scheduling in partnership with the Vice Dean of Academic Affairs, overseeing classroom assignments via EMS and bulk course uploads into Columbia University’s Student Information System (SIS) and Vergil platform.
* Reconcile student enrollment data between internal systems (BORIS/LawNet) and University SIS engines to ensure complete accuracy for billing, residency tracking, and degree audits.
* Consult with University registrar’s office and law school stakeholders to draft academic year calendars, pre\-registration and add/drop calendars.
* Respond to inquiries for various reports. Ensure records are accurately transmitted to the University Registrar.

### **Compliance, Bar Admission \& External Reporting (25%)**


* Serve as the Law School’s primary authority on compliance with ABA Standards (including credit hour verification, distance learning limits, and annual questionnaire filings).
* Direct the certification process for student character, fitness, certificate of attendance, and degree completion for state bar examiners across US jurisdictions, with primary oversight of New York State Bar filings.
* Facilitate data collection and reporting for ABA Student \& Bar Passage Questionnaires and internal institutional research in coordination with other Law School units (including the Business Office and Professional Affairs).

### **Exam Administration, Grading \& Degree Clearance (20%)**


* Oversee year\-round examination administration for J.D., ELL.M., and LL.M.degree programs, ensuring full system integrity, anonymous grading protocols, and accommodation workflows in collaboration with the Office of Disability Services (ODS) and Law School disability liaisons.
* Direct the timely collection of faculty grades, grade curve enforcement, issuance of honors and academic awards.
* Oversee the final J.D., ELL.M., LL.M., and J.S.D graduation clearance process and diploma audits.

### **Departmental Leadership \& Strategic Systems (15%)**


* Manage daily office operations, set departmental goals, and handle budget administration for the office.
* Manage, mentor, and evaluate a team of direct reports within Registration Services.
* Partner with CUIT and Law School IT to audit, modernize, and automate registration technologies (BORIS, LawNet, Vergil).
* Collaborate closely with Student Services, Financial Aid, J.D. and Graduate Program Admissions teams, and Career Services to support seamless student services.
* Serve on ex\-officio administrative and curriculum committees at request to evaluate policy feasibility and academic calendar development.

### **Departmental Support \& Other Duties (10%)**


* Lead cross\-office collaboration during high\-volume periods (registration, exams, orientation, and graduation).
* Perform other related duties as assigned by the Associate Dean to maintain institutional priorities.

Minimum Qualifications


* Bachelor’s degree required; Advanced degree (Master’s, J.D., or equivalent) strongly preferred.
* Minimum of 7 to 9 years of progressive management and supervisory experience in a higher education registrar’s office or academic administration environment (law school setting preferred).

Preferred Qualifications


* Demonstrated knowledge of Student Information Systems (SIS, Banner, or equivalent), registration allocation engines, exam management platforms (e.g., Exam4, ExamSoft), and reporting tools.
* Deep understanding of ABA accreditation requirements, state bar certification rules, and FERPA regulations.
* Exceptional attention to detail, strong oral and written communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to thrive in a high\-volume, fast\-paced environment while managing competing deadlines.
* Must be able to work with diverse constituencies and support an inclusive workplace environment.
* Some evening and weekend work is required during peak operational cycles, specifically during examination periods, add/drop cycles, and bar certification windows

DHS is committed to preventing and addressing homelessness in New York City by employing a variety of innovative strategies to help families and individuals successfully exit shelter and return to self\-sufficiency as quickly as possible.
  

  

Human Resources Solutions (HRS) supports the human resources needs of the Department of Social Services, the Human Resources Administration, and the Department of Homeless Services through strategic partnership and collaboration, with the goal of creating an inclusive, motivated, and client centered workforce.
  

  

The Office of Human Resources Solutions (HRS)/Labor Relations Division is recruiting for an Administrative Director of Social Services M3 to function as the Executive Director of Conflict Resolution, \& Alternative Dispute Resolution Officer, (ADR) who will:
  

  

* Direct the planning, implementation, oversight, and assessment of the Conflict Resolution, Alternative Dispute Resolution, DSS Wellness, and provide assessment for incorporating Employee Relations functions.

  

* Develop and implement agency\-wide initiatives consultation strategies, and training programs addressing workplace conflict, employee relations, behavioral health and wellness, leadership skills, diversity appreciation, and safe and respectful workplaces.

  

* Assess program effectiveness, emerging organizational needs, and service trends, and recommend modifications to programs, protocols, policies, and resource priorities to improve outcomes and align with agency objectives.

* Oversee the assessment and resolution of matters received through multiple entry points, including the Commissioner’s mailbox, anonymous communications, non\-EEO referrals, management referrals, and other channels, and determines the appropriate intervention, coordination, or escalation path.

  

* Respond to significant workplace crises and direct or coordinates management responses. When established procedures are insufficient, develop or recommend protocols and preventive practices for future use.

  

* Supervise Conflict Resolution staff and the DSS Wellness Coordinator. Establishes work priorities, assigns and reviews work, provides technical and managerial direction, evaluates performance, coaches and develop staff, and ensures the quality and timeliness of unit deliverables.

  

* Provide directions to staff responsible for researching, analyzing, reviewing, and disseminating information on agency policy and procedures, employees’ work\-life matters, and organizational responsibilities.

  

* Review agency policies, procedures, and practices within assigned areas to assess their operational applicability, consistency, and impact on organizational performance. Develop recommendations for policy, procedural, or practice changes for executive consideration.

  

* Consult with HR Business Partners, managers, and program leadership on the practical application of employee relations and workplace policies and identifies opportunities to strengthen consistent, fair implementation across the agency.

  

* Use information from conflict resolution, employee relations, wellness, and management consultations to identify recurring or systemic workplace issues and to recommend agency\-wide interventions, management guidance, training, or process improvements.

  

* Develop statistical and management reports to evaluate program activity, identify trends, support planning, and inform executive decision\-making.

jobs.title: Branch Executive Director
jobs.description:
Description:  

The Branch Executive Director provides strategic and operational leadership for an assigned YMCA branch, ensuring excellence in member experience, program quality, financial performance, community impact, and staff development. Reporting to the President \& CEO, this leader is responsible for the overall management of branch operations, including membership growth, program development, fundraising, fiscal stewardship, board and volunteer engagement, and community partnerships. The Executive Director advances the YMCA's mission through Cause\-Driven Leadership and a culture of inclusion, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**1\. Branch Leadership \& Operations**

* Provide overall leadership and management of day\-to\-day branch operations.
* Ensure high\-quality, safe, and mission\-driven programs, services, and facilities.
* Oversee membership engagement, retention, and growth through exceptional customer service and innovative programming.
* Ensure compliance with YMCA policies, risk management standards, and operational procedures.

**2\. Financial Management**

* Develop, manage, and achieve annual operating and capital budgets.
* Monitor financial performance through forecasting, variance analysis, expense management, and revenue growth strategies.
* Ensure sound financial controls and compliance with Association accounting policies.
* Manage reserve accounts and long\-term financial planning.

**3\. Fundraising \& Community Engagement**

* Lead the branch's Annual Giving Campaign and other fundraising initiatives to meet financial development goals.
* Cultivate relationships with donors, community leaders, businesses, foundations, and government partners.
* Represent the YMCA throughout the community while strengthening strategic partnerships and public awareness.

**4\. Staff \& Volunteer Leadership**

* Recruit, develop, supervise, and retain high\-performing staff and volunteers.
* Foster a positive, inclusive workplace culture focused on accountability, professional development, and organizational excellence.
* Conduct performance evaluations, succession planning, and staff development initiatives.

**5\. Board Development \& Governance**

* Partner with the Branch Board of Managers and its committees to advance strategic priorities.
* Support board recruitment, orientation, engagement, and committee effectiveness.
* Provide leadership for strategic planning and annual operational planning.

**6\. Program \& Membership Development**

* Lead the development, evaluation, and continuous improvement of YMCA programs and services.
* Drive membership recruitment, retention, and engagement strategies.
* Expand programs in alignment with community needs and Association priorities.

**7\. Leadership Priorities**

* Provide exceptional leadership for all branch operations.
* Achieve financial, membership, and program performance goals.
* Build strong staff, volunteer, and board leadership.
* Strengthen community partnerships and philanthropic support.
* Foster innovation, operational excellence, and an outstanding member experience.


Requirements:
* Bachelor's degree in Business, Human Services, Recreation, Nonprofit Management, or a related field preferred.
* Five or more years of progressive leadership experience in YMCA, nonprofit, health and wellness, recreation, or comparable business operations.
* Demonstrated success in financial management, fundraising, strategic planning, staff leadership, and operational management.
* Proven ability to develop community partnerships and lead volunteer boards.
* Strong communication, relationship\-building, and decision\-making skills.
* YMCA Multi\-Team Leader Certification preferred or the ability to obtain.
* Ability to respond to operational emergencies and maintain an on\-site leadership presence, including occasional evenings and weekends.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**


This position requires regular on\-site leadership in a dynamic facility environment, including offices, wellness areas, aquatics, youth program spaces, and outdoor locations. The role requires the ability to manage multiple priorities, lift up to 50 pounds, and respond to operational needs as required.

At JPMorganChase, we are investing boldly in transforming how our people work, how teams are organized, and how technology and human capabilities come together to deliver for our customers. jobs.company: The Smith Center for the Arts
jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Smith Center for the Arts in Geneva, NY (“The Smith”) seeks an Executive Director to lead the Finger Lakes region’s premier arts organization.

**The Smith Center for the Arts**

Since 1894, the has thrived as the center stage of the Finger Lakes, offering quality performing arts and cultural opportunities for area residents and regional visitors. With a wide variety of programming that includes live concerts, plays, operas, lectures, films and community events, the theater is an ongoing symbol of historic preservation, non\-profit perseverance and artistic excellence. The Smith is an architectural treasure in a fully restored theater that is air\-conditioned in summer months. The Smith boasts the largest indoor silver screen in the region and now features state\-of\-the\-art digital projection.

**The Executive Director**

The Executive Director leads a dynamic team to continue to provide the highest quality and most diverse artistic programming in the Finger Lakes. The Executive Director is responsible for the consistent realization of the Smith Center for the Arts’ mission and financial goals, as well as the effective management of the staff. The Executive Director, in collaboration with the Board of Directors and staff, is responsible for financial planning, programming, donor relations, marketing and communications. Additionally, the Executive Director works with staff to manage the day\-to\-day operations and facility needs of the Smith Opera House, the beautifully restored 130\-year\-old theatre that is the crown jewel of the Finger Lakes and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

The Smith has an operating budget of over $1 million, and is governed by fourteen Board members. After more nearly a decade leading the organization through one of our most successful eras, during the summer of 2026 the former Executive Director informed the board of the she has accepted a position at a successful arts institution that afforded her the ability to be closer to family. We are seeking a dynamic, visionary Executive Director to lead The Smith during this pivotal transition into its next era.

**Salary and Compensation:**

Anticipated salary range $80\-120,000 commensurate with experience.

**Operations and Facility Responsibilities:**

The Executive Director will serve as the **head of staff**, with all units (including programming, tech, box office, marketing and information, finance, and facilities) reporting to them. As head of staff, the Executive Director will support a healthy and collaborative staff culture grounded in communication, professional development, clarity of roles, and shared purpose. The Executive Director will be responsible for:

\- Overall supervision of staff

\- Recommending staff compensation

\- Annual review of all employees

\- Human Resources management

\- Working with the Business Manager to ensure accurate payment and benefits

The Executive Director will **maintain a close relationship with the Board of Directors**, communicating critical information to help the Board in its decision making. The Executive Director will:

\- Serve on key Board committees

\- Provide an oral report at monthly Board meetings

The Executive Director will set priorities for **buildings and grounds maintenance**, as well as plan and ensure the execution of construction projects. They will steward the historic facility and coordinate with the city and technical leadership on maintenance, capital priorities, infrastructure needs, and operational planning.

The Executive Director will **oversee the day\-to\-day financial health** of The Smith and be responsible for:

\- Approving expenditures

\- Reviewing and approving financial statements

\- Overseeing relationships with banks, auditors, payroll companies, ticketing companies, etc.

\- Overseeing vendor relationships and contracts

**Strategic and Financial Planning**

In collaboration with the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will:

* Work to define and align the organization’s mission with the resources necessary to implement it sustainably
* Develop funding proposals to meet the needs of the organization
* Manage budgeting, annual financial performance, stewardship of assets, and capital planning
* Lead the organization to confidently achieve its short\- and long\-term goals

**Programming**

The Executive Director is responsible for curating programs offered by the Smith Center for the Arts in alignment with the mission, vision, and strategic plan. The Executive Director will:

* Along with designated staff, manage relationships with visiting artists, bill and arrange payment for artists, and write and negotiate contracts
* Develop music, theatre, dance, and film programming from an artistic vision while meeting financial goals
* Demonstrate a strategy for audience development to include an understanding of regional and local draw and a balance for presenting marquee artists as well as community\-based arts groups
* Gather input from all constituents, including but not limited to Geneva’s diverse community, members and patrons, and promoters who follow performance trends
* Seek new programming and revenue streams through creative use of the theatre

**Development and Donor Relations**

Working with the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will oversee the development and implementation of a comprehensive fundraising program. This includes, but is not limited to:

* Directing a program of annual support
* Identifying and cultivating major donor prospects, as well as the stewardship of their gifts, and developing a program of planned giving
* Expanding outreach to foundations, corporations, and municipalities to generate additional revenue, sponsorship, and capital support
* Overseeing a robust program of year\-round events designed to generate revenue

jobs.title: Senior Director of Major Gifts
jobs.description:
Overview:

The Sr. Director of Major Gifts leads the Central Health Foundation’s major\-gifts function and develops and executes strategies to generate significant philanthropic support for Central Health’s mission, strategic priorities, and community impact. Reporting to the Foundation Chief Executive Officer, the Sr. Director manages a portfolio of qualified major\-gift prospects and donors through identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Sr. Director personally solicits significant philanthropic gifts and partners closely with the Foundation CEO on transformational and selected major\-gift opportunities requiring executive involvement. The position establishes disciplined prospect\- and moves\-management practices, develops individualized donor strategies, prepares compelling proposals, and maintains reliable pipeline and revenue forecasts. The Sr. Director leads the execution of the major\-gifts strategy and supports campaign implementation in partnership with Foundation Strategy, which retains responsibility for overarching campaign architecture, strategic prioritization, and organizational readiness. The Sr. Director also works closely with Grants, Annual Giving, Donor Stewardship, Communications, Foundation Operations, Central Health leaders, clinicians, Board members, and community partners to coordinate fundraising activity and donor engagement. The Sr. Director builds and leads the major\-gifts team as approved staffing plans develop. The position may initially operate as a senior individual contributor and player\-coach but is accountable for establishing the structure, practices, performance expectations, and team capacity needed to support a mature major\-gifts program.  

This is a hybrid position. Individuals in this position may work both at an approved off\-site location and onsite at a primary location or multiple locations based on business needs.
Responsibilities:

Essential Functions  

Major\-Gifts Strategy and Portfolio Management:* Develop, implement, and evaluate a multiyear major\-gifts strategy aligned with Central Health priorities, the Foundation’s approved fundraising plan, and overarching campaign architecture.
* Establish annual and multiyear major\-gift revenue goals, pipeline expectations, activity measures, performance indicators, and portfolio standards.
* Personally manage assigned prospects and donors through identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
* Develop individualized donor strategies based on philanthropic interests, giving capacity, readiness, relationship history, and alignment with Foundation priorities.
* Identify and pursue opportunities to increase philanthropic support from individuals, families, corporations, foundations, and other strategic partners.
* Monitor portfolio activity, proposal status, expected revenue, donor movement, relationship ownership, and
* fundraising risks.
* Prepare regular forecasts, performance updates, portfolio analyses, and recommendations for the Foundation CEO and other appropriate leadership audiences.
* Evaluate portfolio distribution and recommend reassignment of prospects as gift officers are hired and the majorgifts function develops.

  

Principal, Transformational, and Executive\-Led Gifts:* Partner with the Foundation CEO to develop and execute strategies for transformational, principal, and selected major\-gift prospects.
* Personally solicit assigned major\-gift prospects and participate in transformational and principal\-gift solicitations with the Foundation CEO and other designated leaders.
* Conduct or coordinate research, donor strategy, relationship mapping, and next\-step planning for CEO\-led and executive\-led relationships.
* Prepare the Foundation CEO, Board members, Central Health executives, clinicians, and community leaders for donor meetings and solicitations.
* Develop briefing materials, talking points, proposals, presentations, solicitation strategies, and follow\-up plans for significant gift opportunities.
* Coordinate the participation of executives, Board members, clinicians, volunteers, and other relationship partners in donor engagement.
* Clarify relationship ownership, solicitation roles, decision points, timelines, and follow\-up responsibilities.
* Track commitments and next steps associated with transformational, principal, and major\-gift strategies.


Campaign Execution and Case Development:* Lead major\-gifts execution within the Foundation’s broader campaign and fundraising strategy.
* Partner with Foundation Strategy, which leads overarching campaign architecture, funding themes, initiative sequencing, readiness requirements, and strategic prioritization.
* Provide donor\-market, portfolio, and pipeline insight to inform campaign priorities, feasibility, leadership engagement, solicitation planning, and fundraising goals.
* Participate substantially in prospect strategy and solicitation planning.
* Assess campaign readiness from a fundraising perspective, including prospect strength, donor interest, volunteer leadership, case development, and stewardship capacity.
* Develop or coordinate cases for support, donor proposals, initiative summaries, presentations, and solicitation materials.
* Partner with Foundation Strategy, Communications, Strategic Alignment and Impact, Foundation Operations, and Central Health leaders to ensure donor materials accurately reflect approved organizational priorities, budgets, outcomes, readiness, and community impact.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to the CEO
jobs.description:
**Executive Assistant to the CEO**

**Raphah Institute \| Nashville, Tennessee \| Full time \| Nonexempt**


Raphah Institute is seeking an Executive Assistant to the CEO to build dependable coordination around the CEO’s work. This person will help keep meetings, commitments, schedules, information, and follow\-through moving so the CEO can devote more attention to organizational leadership, fundraising, governance, and strategic relationships.


The role begins with close collaboration and grows into ownership of defined executive support workflows. We are looking for someone who enjoys creating order around complex work, closes loops reliably, and knows when a decision belongs with the CEO or another organizational leader.

**What you will do**
====================

* Coordinate the CEO’s calendar, meeting invitations, scheduling conflicts, preparation time, and travel within agreed priorities.
* Capture and track follow\-ups, introductions, approvals, requested documents, and other CEO commitments through completion.
* Prepare meeting logistics, relevant materials, concise first\-pass briefs, and post\-meeting action lists.
* Support executive correspondence, board\-related administration, travel arrangements, and document routing.
* Organize information from email, calendar, meeting notes, and approved systems so time\-sensitive matters reach the CEO promptly.
* Document and improve recurring executive workflows, using approved productivity and AI tools with careful verification and confidentiality practices.
* Coordinate administrative handoffs with colleagues, board members, funders, partners, and advisors while preserving their decision authority.

**What you bring**
==================

* Experience coordinating multiple schedules, requests, documents, or commitments in a complex environment.
* Excellent follow\-through, organization, written communication, and attention to detail.
* Sound judgment about confidential information and about when to act, seek approval, or escalate.
* Confidence with digital productivity tools and willingness to learn new systems, including responsible uses of AI.
* Ability to work respectfully and effectively with senior stakeholders and colleagues across an organization.
* Interest in building dependable processes and improving them over time.


Experience supporting a senior leader, coordinating board logistics, or working in a nonprofit is welcome but not required. We value demonstrated capability and equivalent combinations of education, work, and practical experience.

**Position details**
====================


This is a full\-time, on\-site position at Raphah Institute’s Nashville office, generally 40 hours per week. The position reports to the CEO and has no supervisory responsibility. It is classified internally as a Level 2 Executive Operations Coordinator in the Operations, People \& Systems job family.


The CEO\-approved hiring range for this Nashville Level 2 position is $27\.88–$34\.62 per hour, equivalent to approximately $58,000–$72,000 for 2,080 straight\-time hours. Placement within the range will reflect relevant experience, demonstrated capability, internal equity, and Raphah Institute’s compensation practices. The position is nonexempt; hours worked must be recorded and overtime is administered in accordance with applicable law and organizational policy.


The position is eligible for Raphah Institute’s benefits for full\-time employees, subject to the terms and eligibility requirements of the applicable plans. Benefit details will be provided during the hiring process.

**About Raphah Institute**
==========================


Raphah Institute works to transform harm into lasting safety through relational accountability, community repair, and durable stability. Visit https://www.raphah.org/ for more information.

**Equal opportunity and accessibility**
=======================================


Raphah Institute is committed to nondiscrimination in employment. No person will be excluded from consideration, denied employment opportunities, or otherwise subjected to discrimination in Raphah Institute’s employment practices on the grounds of disability, age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, or any other classification protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to participate in the application process and perform the essential functions of the position.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
**About JM Test Systems**


JM Test Systems provides calibration, test and measurement equipment, and technical services across multiple business segments and service locations. We help customers in industrial, energy, manufacturing, and other demanding environments keep critical instruments accurate, compliant, and ready to perform.

**Job Summary — The Opportunity**


Our network of locations is where JM Test Systems delivers for customers every day, in our labs, on our rental floors, and in the field. As we grow, both organically and through acquisitions, we're looking for a Director of Operations to bring our locations together into one consistent, scalable operation.


In this role, you will restructure and standardize how our growing locations operate, integrate newly acquired businesses, and build the foundation that lets us scale, all while driving profitability, revenue growth, turnaround times, safety, and customer satisfaction. You'll partner with our Chief Revenue Officer, Director of Marketing, and division managers to grow market share, sharpen pricing and service offerings, and bring in the processes and technology that help our teams work smarter.


You'll thrive here if you're a strategic, data\-driven leader who develops strong teams, stays close to customers, and has built consistency and scale across a growing, multi\-location business.

**Key Responsibilities \& Outcomes**

* **Standardize for scale.** Restructure operations across our locations to create consistent processes, structures, and standards that support continued growth.
* **Integrate acquisitions.** Lead the operational integration of newly acquired businesses, bringing their people, processes, and systems into the JM Test Systems way of working.
* **Drive financial performance.** Deliver EBITDA and revenue to plan across all locations through smart pricing, expanded service offerings, sales strategies, and cost control.
* **Grow market share.** Work with the CRO and Director of Marketing on digital strategy, new market segments, product category management, strategic partnerships, and brand visibility.
* **Delight customers.** Improve customer satisfaction and loyalty through regular surveys, feedback, faster turnaround, and prompt issue resolution.
* **Make operations more efficient.** Streamline processes, automate tasks, implement technology, and optimize resources to improve order fulfillment and calibration and repair turnaround times.
* **Lead a safety\-first culture.** Ensure every location meets safety programs, audits, and inspections, and stays compliant with industry regulations and company policies.
* **Build high\-performing teams.** Set clear goals, coach and develop leaders, recognize performance, and improve engagement and retention across the network.

**What You Bring**

* **Required:** MBA or a similar advanced degree in business or a related field.
* **Required:** Proven experience leading operations across multiple locations, with accountability for P\&L, EBITDA, and revenue results.
* **Required:** Track record of standardizing and scaling a growing multi\-location business, including integrating acquisitions.
* **Required:** Strong business and financial insight, with the ability to use data and market trends to guide pricing, service offerings, and strategy.
* **Required:** Track record of improving efficiency, turnaround times, and customer satisfaction through process and technology, and of developing talent and building engaged teams.
* **Required:** Excellent communication and relationship\-building skills with customers, leaders, and teams at every level.
* **Preferred:** Experience in rental, calibration, testing, or industrial services.

**Why JM Test Systems?**


This is a senior leadership role with a direct impact on how JM Test Systems grows. You'll work alongside our executive team, lead across a network of locations and service lines, and have the ownership to build the operating model that carries us through our next stage of growth.

**Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* HSA with employer contribution
* Paid time off and company holidays
* 401(k) retirement plan with company matching
* Company\-paid life insurance
* Supplemental insurance policies
* Training and development opportunities
* Opportunities for continued growth within JM Test Systems

**Equal Opportunity Employer**




JM Test Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

The above hiring range represents the University's good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting.*  

Position Summary


Reporting to the Associate Dean of Students and Registration Services, the Executive Director and Registrar serves as the lead administrator for the Office of Registration Services (ORS) at Columbia Law School. The Registrar leads a dedicated team of higher education professionals responsible for academic policy implementation, registration operations, recordkeeping, exam administration, grade tracking, graduation clearance, and strict regulatory compliance (including ABA standards, NYS Bar requirements, and FERPA). Working closely with the Office of the Vice Dean of Academic Affairs, the Office of Student Services, the Office of Graduate Degree Programs and other Law School and University partners, the Registrar ensures data integrity across institutional databases while driving digital transformation to enhance student\-facing and administrative workflows to ensure a positive, efficient, and professional student learning experience.


Responsibilities


**Academic Operations \& Registration Management (30%)**


* Lead biannual registration, course lottery allocations, cross\-registration (including Columbia Graduate Schools such as Columbia Business School (CBS) and the School for International and Public Affairs (SIPA), and the Columbia/NYU Exchange Program)), and add/drop processes.
* Manage course setup and scheduling in partnership with the Vice Dean of Academic Affairs, overseeing classroom assignments via EMS and bulk course uploads into Columbia University’s Student Information System (SIS) and Vergil platform.
* Reconcile student enrollment data between internal systems (BORIS/LawNet) and University SIS engines to ensure complete accuracy for billing, residency tracking, and degree audits.
* Consult with University registrar’s office and law school stakeholders to draft academic year calendars, pre\-registration and add/drop calendars.
* Respond to inquiries for various reports. Ensure records are accurately transmitted to the University Registrar.

### **Compliance, Bar Admission \& External Reporting (25%)**


* Serve as the Law School’s primary authority on compliance with ABA Standards (including credit hour verification, distance learning limits, and annual questionnaire filings).
* Direct the certification process for student character, fitness, certificate of attendance, and degree completion for state bar examiners across US jurisdictions, with primary oversight of New York State Bar filings.
* Facilitate data collection and reporting for ABA Student \& Bar Passage Questionnaires and internal institutional research in coordination with other Law School units (including the Business Office and Professional Affairs).

### **Exam Administration, Grading \& Degree Clearance (20%)**


* Oversee year\-round examination administration for J.D., ELL.M., and LL.M.degree programs, ensuring full system integrity, anonymous grading protocols, and accommodation workflows in collaboration with the Office of Disability Services (ODS) and Law School disability liaisons.
* Direct the timely collection of faculty grades, grade curve enforcement, issuance of honors and academic awards.
* Oversee the final J.D., ELL.M., LL.M., and J.S.D graduation clearance process and diploma audits.

### **Departmental Leadership \& Strategic Systems (15%)**


* Manage daily office operations, set departmental goals, and handle budget administration for the office.
* Manage, mentor, and evaluate a team of direct reports within Registration Services.
* Partner with CUIT and Law School IT to audit, modernize, and automate registration technologies (BORIS, LawNet, Vergil).
* Collaborate closely with Student Services, Financial Aid, J.D. and Graduate Program Admissions teams, and Career Services to support seamless student services.
* Serve on ex\-officio administrative and curriculum committees at request to evaluate policy feasibility and academic calendar development.

### **Departmental Support \& Other Duties (10%)**


* Lead cross\-office collaboration during high\-volume periods (registration, exams, orientation, and graduation).
* Perform other related duties as assigned by the Associate Dean to maintain institutional priorities.

Minimum Qualifications


* Bachelor’s degree required; Advanced degree (Master’s, J.D., or equivalent) strongly preferred.
* Minimum of 7 to 9 years of progressive management and supervisory experience in a higher education registrar’s office or academic administration environment (law school setting preferred).

Preferred Qualifications


* Demonstrated knowledge of Student Information Systems (SIS, Banner, or equivalent), registration allocation engines, exam management platforms (e.g., Exam4, ExamSoft), and reporting tools.
* Deep understanding of ABA accreditation requirements, state bar certification rules, and FERPA regulations.
* Exceptional attention to detail, strong oral and written communication skills, and a demonstrated ability to thrive in a high\-volume, fast\-paced environment while managing competing deadlines.
* Must be able to work with diverse constituencies and support an inclusive workplace environment.
* Some evening and weekend work is required during peak operational cycles, specifically during examination periods, add/drop cycles, and bar certification windows

new_jobs.title: Branch Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
Description:  

The Branch Executive Director provides strategic and operational leadership for an assigned YMCA branch, ensuring excellence in member experience, program quality, financial performance, community impact, and staff development. Reporting to the President \& CEO, this leader is responsible for the overall management of branch operations, including membership growth, program development, fundraising, fiscal stewardship, board and volunteer engagement, and community partnerships. The Executive Director advances the YMCA's mission through Cause\-Driven Leadership and a culture of inclusion, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**1\. Branch Leadership \& Operations**

* Provide overall leadership and management of day\-to\-day branch operations.
* Ensure high\-quality, safe, and mission\-driven programs, services, and facilities.
* Oversee membership engagement, retention, and growth through exceptional customer service and innovative programming.
* Ensure compliance with YMCA policies, risk management standards, and operational procedures.

**2\. Financial Management**

* Develop, manage, and achieve annual operating and capital budgets.
* Monitor financial performance through forecasting, variance analysis, expense management, and revenue growth strategies.
* Ensure sound financial controls and compliance with Association accounting policies.
* Manage reserve accounts and long\-term financial planning.

**3\. Fundraising \& Community Engagement**

* Lead the branch's Annual Giving Campaign and other fundraising initiatives to meet financial development goals.
* Cultivate relationships with donors, community leaders, businesses, foundations, and government partners.
* Represent the YMCA throughout the community while strengthening strategic partnerships and public awareness.

**4\. Staff \& Volunteer Leadership**

* Recruit, develop, supervise, and retain high\-performing staff and volunteers.
* Foster a positive, inclusive workplace culture focused on accountability, professional development, and organizational excellence.
* Conduct performance evaluations, succession planning, and staff development initiatives.

**5\. Board Development \& Governance**

* Partner with the Branch Board of Managers and its committees to advance strategic priorities.
* Support board recruitment, orientation, engagement, and committee effectiveness.
* Provide leadership for strategic planning and annual operational planning.

**6\. Program \& Membership Development**

* Lead the development, evaluation, and continuous improvement of YMCA programs and services.
* Drive membership recruitment, retention, and engagement strategies.
* Expand programs in alignment with community needs and Association priorities.

**7\. Leadership Priorities**

* Provide exceptional leadership for all branch operations.
* Achieve financial, membership, and program performance goals.
* Build strong staff, volunteer, and board leadership.
* Strengthen community partnerships and philanthropic support.
* Foster innovation, operational excellence, and an outstanding member experience.


Requirements:
* Bachelor's degree in Business, Human Services, Recreation, Nonprofit Management, or a related field preferred.
* Five or more years of progressive leadership experience in YMCA, nonprofit, health and wellness, recreation, or comparable business operations.
* Demonstrated success in financial management, fundraising, strategic planning, staff leadership, and operational management.
* Proven ability to develop community partnerships and lead volunteer boards.
* Strong communication, relationship\-building, and decision\-making skills.
* YMCA Multi\-Team Leader Certification preferred or the ability to obtain.
* Ability to respond to operational emergencies and maintain an on\-site leadership presence, including occasional evenings and weekends.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**


This position requires regular on\-site leadership in a dynamic facility environment, including offices, wellness areas, aquatics, youth program spaces, and outdoor locations. The role requires the ability to manage multiple priorities, lift up to 50 pounds, and respond to operational needs as required.
